caption: WER during fine-tuning Whisper model with different types of fine-tunning
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the Word Error Rate (WER) over epochs during full fine-tuning of the Whisper model, comparing two configurations: “tiny full” (gray triangles connected by a dotted line) and “base full” (blue triangles connected by a dashed line). The x-axis, labeled “epoch,” ranges from 0 to 6 with integer tick marks, representing training progress. The y-axis, labeled “WER,” spans from approximately 19 to 29, with major grid lines at intervals of 2. The “tiny full” model starts at a WER of ~28.7 at epoch 0, drops sharply to ~24.1 by epoch 3, then gradually declines to ~22.8 by epoch 6. The “base full” model begins at ~21.9, dips to ~20.9 at epoch 1, rises slightly to ~21.3 at epoch 2, then steadily decreases to ~18.9 by epoch 6. Both models show overall improvement in WER over training, with the “base full” model consistently achieving lower error rates than the “tiny full” model across all epochs.
